clue.text: Will may have had four instances of these

definitions.text: Will may have had four instances of these

parts.words: Will may have had four instances of these
parts.note: read 'Will may have had' as a list rather than a sentence: will, may, have and had are all helper verbs used with a main verb

explanation.surface: Someone called Will apparently owned four examples of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a man's name (or a testament), but the first four words are simply four examples of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Will, may, have and had are grammar's helping verbs, which combine with a main verb to show tense or mood.

clue.text: A typical ball he tossed in order that most of us follow

definitions.text: in order that most of us follow

indicators.note: letters that are tossed about land in a new arrangement, so the preceding words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A standard ball is thrown by a player in the usual sequence of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges all the letters of A TYPICAL BALL HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Most readers of English follow A-to-Z ordering, as in dictionaries and indexes, so this adverb describes that familiar order.

clue.text: Investigative job, one in Glasgow, in Times newspaper

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

indicators.note: the Scots word for one is placed in the middle of the word for a newspaper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
yin is the Scots word for one, as spoken in Glasgow

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian reporter does an investigation for The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's Times is the newspaper, but here it is the multiplication sign; 'yin' is Scots dialect for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiographic imaging is an investigative procedure in medicine, looking inside the body to find what is wrong.

clue.text: Shelter chief doctor of old

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: The head of a refuge was once a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicians were once called by this name, from the Old English word for healer, as well as for their bloodsucking worms.

clue.text: Where flier's managed to drop in relief?

definitions.text: Where flier's managed to drop in relief?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters drop into the middle of the word for relief

parts.note: aid is help or relief

indicators.note: managed in the sense of handled or worked over, so the letters of flier are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot is relieved to have landed safely somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a pilot comes down, relieved, at such a place.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is where aircraft land, so a pilot who has come down safely has done so there.

clue.text: Yankee regularly reeled in one's profits

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the alternate letters go inside the letters for one's

parts.note: I'S: I for one, plus the 's

indicators.note: taking every other letter of reeled, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An American angler reels in his profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of reeled, giving ELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns on an investment are its yields, so the plural noun means gains or earnings.

clue.text: Anticipating men avoiding cough medicine?

indicators.note: the word for cough medicine avoids, so goes without, the letters for men

parts.note: an expectorant is a medicine that helps bring up phlegm
OR (other ranks) is a crossword term for ordinary soldiers, or men

explanation.surface: Is someone hoping men will stop taking their cough syrup?
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes OR from EXPECTORANT. OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in hopeful waiting for something is to be expectant, so the adjective matches anticipating.

clue.text: Blondin needed this money in the bank

definitions.meaning: Charles Blondin was the tightrope walker who crossed Niagara Falls, a feat requiring steadiness on the rope
the amount held in an account

explanation.surface: A famous stuntman relied on his savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Blondin was a 19th-century French tightrope walker famous for crossing Niagara Falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Equilibrium kept a tightrope walker upright, and the same word names the sum in one's bank account.

clue.text: Stop fighting that butchery he spread

indicators.note: the letters of the words are spread out and laid down in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's violent slaughter has spread and must end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges the letters of THAT BUTCHERY HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from Native American custom of laying down a tomahawk, meaning to make peace and end a quarrel.

clue.text: Intend to be in Paris to tour energy plant

parts.note: to plan is to intend

indicators.note: the French verb goes around, or tours, the letter for energy

parts.note: être is French for to be
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone means to be in Paris to visit a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' puts E inside ETRE, giving ETREE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large tree, the London plane, so it is a kind of plant in the botanical sense; the surface makes 'plant' a factory.

clue.text: Bend a rim around dish

indicators.note: the three pieces, taken together, are turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a U-bend, so U
a lip is a rim, as of a cup

explanation.surface: Instructions to curve the edge of a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses ULIP as a whole to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced rice preparation of the Middle East and South Asia, a well-known example of a dish.

clue.text: This writer's about to chop wood for people associated with PA

indicators.note: the reversed pair cuts into the word for wood, splitting it

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

indicators.note: the letters for this writer's are turned about, read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to himself: I'm, this writer is

explanation.surface: An author is about to cut up some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses IM to MI, and 'to chop' puts it inside ASH. PA is the abbreviation for Pennsylvania.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anabaptist community, known for plain dress and horse-drawn buggies, is strongly identified with Pennsylvania.

clue.text: One month enclosed in city leads to lewd behaviour

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the month and the enclosure abbreviation sit in the city letters

parts.note: NY is New York city
DEC is short for December
ENC is the abbreviation written on letters for enclosed

explanation.surface: A month cooped up in a city drives one to obscene acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' looks like the insertion signal but is the letter abbreviation enc.; 'in' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd conduct offends public standards of propriety, which is what the noun names.

clue.text: Finish, say, golf round

parts.note: e.g. means for example, signalled by say
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a shell is a round of artillery ammunition

explanation.surface: Wrap up, for example, a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A paint finish with a slight sheen, named after the surface of a bird's egg, so it is a kind of finish.

clue.text: Ambassador dealing with foreign articles later

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
re means concerning or dealing with
un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite one, joined together

explanation.surface: A diplomat handles imported goods afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The article in 'foreign articles' is the grammar sort, not a thing: UN (French) and DER (German).
explanation.definitionFit: In legal documents the word means below or subsequently in this text, so it points to what comes later.

clue.text: Israeli character halted round the bend

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters of halted go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: An Israeli person stopped at a corner of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' rearranges HALTED.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, used in Israel, so it is a written character.

clue.text: Go along with gunmen to capture a monster

indicators.note: the word for go along with captures, so contains, the a

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

explanation.surface: Agree to join armed men in catching a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunmen are the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners, not criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-breathing beast of Greek myth, part lion, part goat and part serpent.

clue.text: Detain the latest flyer

parts.note: in means fashionable, the latest thing
a tern is a seabird, a flyer

explanation.surface: Hold the most recent bird or pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone, especially in wartime without trial, is to detain them.

clue.text: Bird caught in a mountain, wings clipped

indicators.note: the outer letters of the run caught in a mountain are cut away at each side, leaving the letters inside

explanation.surface: A bird trapped on a peak has had its wings cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings clipped' trims caugh- and -ntain from CAUGHT IN A MOUNTAIN. 'caught' looks like a hidden word signal or C, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground-dwelling South and Central American game species, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Chat up drunk husband round rear of Ritz? The cheek!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the end of Ritz
a drunk jumbles things, so the letters are rearranged
the rear of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy married man flirts outside a luxury hotel, and what a nerve!
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns CHAT UP into CHUTPA; 'round' puts it round Z, the 'rear of' Ritz, giving CHUTZPA, then H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yiddish word for audacity or nerve, so it matches the exclamation about impudence.

clue.text: Border stitch that is initially unravelling

parts.note: purl is a knitting stitch
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: only the first letter of unravelling is taken

explanation.surface: A knitter's edging stitch is starting to come undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' looks like an anagram signal, but 'initially' takes only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The outskirts or fringe of a place is called this, so it means an edge or border area.

clue.text: Not as busy, having this class?

parts.note: less means not as much
on means occupied or in use, as a line that is busy

explanation.surface: Was having this lesson less demanding?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words: less on, not as much going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A school period of teaching is a class, a session where pupils are taught.

clue.text: Plug new gold vein until all are bored

parts.note: a plug is an advert, an ad
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a seam is a vein of ore or coal

explanation.surface: Keep promoting a newly found gold seam until everyone's weary of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning to the point of sickness, describing something repeated endlessly until it tires everyone.

clue.text: Bordeaux leaking litres, a sign something's missing

indicators.note: the wine is leaking, so losing, the letter for litres

parts.note: claret is red wine from Bordeaux

explanation.surface: A wine bottle losing its contents shows something's gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaking' removes L from CLARET.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders use this wedge-shaped mark to show where text needs inserting, signalling an omission.

clue.text: Officer in charge of early complaint

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer has a grievance from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe crying with abdominal pain in young babies is this ailment, so it is a complaint of early life.

clue.text: Given some whitewash, being restricted without it

indicators.note: the word for restricted goes without, so loses, the letters of it

parts.note: limited means restricted

explanation.surface: A cover-up report was limited in scope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes IT from LIMITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitewash is made of slaked calcium, and coating a surface with it is to treat it with that substance.

clue.text: Seafood from Hull is served in fine hotel

parts.note: a hull is the outer shell or husk, as of a pea

indicators.note: is is served in, placed between, the letters for fine and hotel

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Seafood from the Yorkshire port is on the menu at a smart hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, but here it means an outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, prawns and mussels are sea creatures eaten as food, so this word is a type of seafood.

clue.text: Electricity bill that attracts little or no interest?

definitions.text: that attracts little or no interest?

parts.note: an electric current is a flow of electricity
an account is a bill to be paid

explanation.surface: An energy invoice that nobody bothers to read.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'interest' is curiosity; the definition's interest is what a bank pays.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday bank accounts for paying in and out typically pay little or nothing in interest.
